subject: Next steps: Aegis eval on Redwood (dataset format & scoring)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Michael O'Connor <m.oconnor@aegispharma.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps: Aegis eval on Redwood (dataset format & scoring)

Michael — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off a customer-specific eval on Redwood: 

Summary of ask
- Primary use case: clinical summarization + triage for incoming provider notes (sensitivity to hallucination and omission).
- Success criteria you emphasized: high factual precision on medication/procedure extraction, recall on critical condition flags, and no PII leakage.

Redwood-recommended starting models & runtime config
- Candidate models to try (we'll run comparatives): Mistral-7B-8k-fp16, LlamaX-13B-q8, and a Redwood-fine-tuned 7B variant optimized for clinical prompts (RF-Clin7B-8k).
- Suggested runtime: fp16 for Mistral, q8/q4 variants for LlamaX depending on token budget. We’ll include a quantized variant to demonstrate cost/latency tradeoffs.

Evaluation plan & deliverables
- We will run three benchmark passes: (1) token-level hallucination check, (2) structured extraction (meds/procedures) scoring, (3) end-to-end clinical summary quality (automated + human sample).
- Deliverables: per-model scorecard, prompt-set sensitivity matrix, cost/latency per 1k tokens, and a short quality-regression analysis against your current baseline.

Data / upload instructions
- Preferred format: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL). Each record should be a single JSON object with keys: id, source_text, reference_summary (optional), labels (array of objects). We included a sample file and an evaluation_template.csv to show mapping. Please avoid including raw MRNs/SSNs; if present, mark as REDACTED.
- Upload options: share folder (recommended): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEXAMPLE or sftp if you prefer.

Scoring rubric (draft)
- Structured extraction: token-level F1 for entities (medications, doses, procedures) + exact-match for flags.
- Summary quality: ROUGE-L + 5-point human rating on factuality (1=major errors, 5=no errors).
- Overall pass threshold: structured extraction F1 >= 0.85 and mean factuality rating >= 4.0 for acceptance into a pilot.

Timeline & next steps
- Confirm dataset upload by EOD Mon (11/16) -> we spin up eval run, deliver initial scorecards within 3 business days.
- Proposed kickoff: 45-minute eval-onboarding session with your engineering and privacy contacts. Ben will coordinate scheduling.

Attachments: evaluation_template.csv, prompt_set_v1.txt, sample_records.jsonl (sample schema + 10 records).

Let me know if this matches your expectations or if you want us to include any additional checks (e.g., entity linking, PHI-detection).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Michael O'Connor <m.oconnor@aegispharma.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sonal Patel <sonal.patel@aegispharma.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: Aegis eval on Redwood (dataset format & scoring)

Laura — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying points before we upload: 

1) PII / de-id: we do have a staged dataset with patient identifiers removed, but some records still contain provider initials. Is that acceptable if we mark those fields as REDACTED?
2) Scoring weights: for us, meds/procedures extraction is higher priority than general summarization. Can we set extraction weight = 0.7 and summary = 0.3 in the first pass?
3) Negative sampling: Sonal asked whether we can include a set of adversarial/noise cases (abbreviations, shorthand) to stress-test hallucinations.

Also cc'ing Sonal (our lead NLP engineer) to confirm timeline availability for the kickoff. We'll aim to have the dataset ready by Monday but want to confirm the schema will be OK.

-Michael
Michael O'Connor
Head of Data Science | Aegis Pharma
m.oconnor@aegispharma.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Michael O'Connor <m.oconnor@aegispharma.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sonal Patel <sonal.patel@aegispharma.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: Aegis eval on Redwood (dataset format & scoring)

Michael / Sonal — we can absolutely accept REDACTED placeholders for provider initials; that meets our de-id guidance.

On weights: noted — we'll configure the automated scoring to apply 0.7 weight to structured extraction metrics and 0.3 to summary scores for the initial pass. We'll include a sensitivity run that sweeps weights so you can see stability.

Negative sampling: yes — please include a folder called "adversarial_cases" inside the upload with 200-500 records (or fewer if that's what you have). We'll run a targeted hallucination report against that set.

Kickoff scheduling: Ben here — proposing Mon 11/16 10:00-10:45 PST or Tue 11/17 09:00-09:45 PST. Which works for your team? I'll send a calendar invite and attach the evaluation rubric draft (pdf).

Regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Michael O'Connor <m.oconnor@aegispharma.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sonal Patel <sonal.patel@aegispharma.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: Aegis eval on Redwood (dataset format & scoring)

Thanks all — quick confirmations and a small schema snippet below that you can copy into your pipeline. We also uploaded sample_records.jsonl to the shared Drive.

Schema (JSONL per line):
{"id": "string", "source_text": "string", "reference_summary": "string (optional)", "labels": [{"entity_type": "medication|procedure|flag", "start": integer, "end": integer, "text": "string", "normalized": "string (optional)"}], "metadata": {"redacted": true}}

Prompt guidance (prompt_set_v1.txt attached): use a two-shot clinical instruction with explicit extraction schema. Example: 
System: You are a clinical assistant. Extract medications (name, dose), procedures, and flags (critical).
User: "{source_text}"
Assistant: JSON with keys medications, procedures, flags.

Evaluation notes on regression risk: 
- Because you’ll be testing quantized variants, small factuality regressions are possible on low-frequency tokens (dosage units). We’ll flag regressions by token class and provide a per-entity error breakdown so you can decide if a quantized candidate is acceptable.

I'll attach the evaluation_template.csv (column mapping), prompt_set_v1.txt, and sample_records.jsonl in the drive folder. If Monday works, Ben, please send the invite and we'll loop in our privacy officer as needed.

Laura
